timeline.title: Investigation Launched into Alaska Senate Candidate Over Alleged Spoiler Scheme
timeline.summary: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign. This follows allegations that her campaign recruited a second candidate named Dan Sullivan to confuse voters and dilute support for the incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan. Donald Trump has also called for Peltola's prosecution over these claims.
key_facts: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation into Mary Peltola's campaign.
The investigation is based on allegations of recruiting a candidate with the same name as incumbent Dan Sullivan.
Donald Trump has called for Peltola's prosecution regarding the alleged scheme.

timeline.title: Mary Peltola Secures Senate Seat in Alaska, Defeating Incumbent Dan Sullivan
timeline.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola has won the Alaska Senate race, defeating incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan. This victory marks a significant shift in the Senate, giving Democrats a 56-44 majority after a series of midterm elections where they flipped nine Republican-held seats. Peltola's win is particularly notable in a state that has historically supported Donald Trump.
key_facts: Mary Peltola won the Alaska Senate race.
She defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan.
This victory gives Democrats a 56-44 majority in the Senate.
Peltola's win is part of a broader trend where Democrats flipped nine GOP-held seats.

event_overview.title: About Alaska Senate Race
event_overview.subject: Alaska Senate Race
event_overview.summary: The Alaska Senate race was the 2026 statewide election for Alaska’s Class II seat in the U.S. Senate, held during the federal midterm cycle. It featured incumbent Republican Dan S. Sullivan and former Democratic U.S. Rep. Mary Peltola, alongside other candidates advancing from Alaska’s nonpartisan top-four primary; the contest was conducted under the state’s ranked-choice general-election system.

facts.label: Office and election cycle
facts.value: Alaskans elect a U.S. senator for this seat every six years; the seat held by Dan Sullivan was a Class II Senate seat with a term scheduled to expire in 2027 before the 2026 election.

facts.label: Date and jurisdiction
facts.value: The statewide general election was held on November 3, 2026, and was administered by the Alaska Division of Elections.

facts.label: Election format
facts.value: Alaska used a single top-four primary followed by ranked-choice voting in the general election: voters could rank the four advancing candidates, and tabulation proceeds through eliminations if no candidate wins a majority of first-choice votes.

facts.label: General-election field
facts.value: The Senate ballot listed Mary Peltola, incumbent Dan S. Sullivan, Gerald L. Heikes, and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.; a candidate’s listed affiliation did not itself constitute party nomination or endorsement.

facts.label: Results status as of November 18, 2026
facts.value: The Division of Elections characterized its posted general-election results as unofficial and scheduled ranked-choice tabulations for November 18 after eligible ballots had been reviewed and counted.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows several prominent campaign and post-election developments, including debate issues, allegations concerning another candidate’s entry, and the reported outcome; it does not constitute a complete account of the race, vote count, litigation, or certification process.
